title: Gaudo Island in Gangjin: Korea's Walkable Island Hideaway on the South Coast (Beginner's Guide)
html:
Most first-time visitors to Korea never make it past Seoul and Busan — which is exactly why Gaudo Island (가우도, "Gau-do") in Gangjin, Jeollanam-do, feels like such a find. It's a tiny, car-free island you reach by walking across a suspension bridge, with an easy coastal trail, a zip line, and some of the calmest bay views on Korea's south coast. If you're road-tripping through the southwest (Jeollanam-do) region, it's a perfect half-day stop.

Gaudo Island and its suspension bridge. Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI, visitkorea.or.kr)

What is Gaudo Island?

Gaudo Island sits inside Gangjinman Bay, a wide, sheltered bay in Jeollanam-do (South Jeolla Province), one of Korea's less-visited southwestern provinces. It's the only one of eight small islands in the bay that people actually live on. The name comes from the island's shape — locals say it looks like the curved wooden yoke ("meonge" in Korean) that farmers used to put around a cow's neck to pull a plow, because the nearby mountain looks like a cow's head.

You don't need a boat to get here. Gaudo is connected to the mainland by two pedestrian suspension bridges (one on each side), so you simply walk across. There are no cars on the island itself — just the walking trail, a handful of cafés and rest areas, and the activities below.

Gangjinman Bay as seen from the island. Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI, visitkorea.or.kr)

Walking the island: the coastal trail

Once you cross the bridge, a 2.5-kilometer (about 1.5-mile) ecological trail loops around the island, hugging the coastline and climbing partway up the hillside. It's a flat, easy walk — comfortable sneakers are fine, no hiking boots needed — and most people finish the full loop in under an hour, longer if you stop often for photos. Along the way you'll pass pine and magnolia groves, small fishing-themed sculptures, and benches facing the water. Because the island is so small, it's almost impossible to get lost; every path eventually loops back.

Part of the 2.5 km walking trail. Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI, visitkorea.or.kr)

The Cheongja Tower and zip line

Near the highest point of the island stands the Cheongja Tower ("cheongja" means "celadon," the famous blue-green Korean pottery). That's not a random name — Gangjin is one of Korea's most important historic centers for making goryeo celadon, a style of ceramic that dates back nearly a thousand years, and the tower design nods to that local heritage.

From the base of the 25-meter (about 82-foot) tower, there's a zip line that carries you out over the water back toward the mainland side. According to the Korea Tourism Organization's listing, it runs daily from 09:00 to 18:00, and fees were listed around 25,000 won for individuals (roughly $18–19 USD), with lower group and student rates. Prices and hours at small local attractions like this can shift from season to season, so it's worth double-checking with the Gangjin County tourism office or a Korean map app (Naver Map or Kakao Map) on the day you go.

Cheongja Tower, starting point of the zip line. Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI, visitkorea.or.kr)

Fishing park and the view back across the bay

On the side of the island facing the open bay, there's a small fishing park where you can rent gear and try your luck — it's popular with Korean families on weekends, more for the relaxed vibe than serious fishing. Even if you don't fish, it's one of the best spots on the island to just sit, watch the tide move across the mud flats, and take in the string of uninhabited islets scattered across Gangjinman Bay. Sunset here, with the water catching the light, is a quieter version of the famous coastal views Korea's bigger islands are known for.

The fishing park, overlooking Gangjinman Bay. Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI, visitkorea.or.kr)

How to get there

Gaudo Island is remote enough that it only makes sense as part of a longer Jeollanam-do road trip or a stop on the way to/from Gangjin's other sights (like the Goryeo celadon kiln sites). There's no train station nearby, so plan around buses:

  • From Seoul: Take the KTX (Korea's high-speed train) from Seoul Station to Gwangju Songjeong Station (about 2 hours). From there, transfer to the subway to reach Gwangju's intercity bus terminal, then take an intercity bus bound for Gangjin (roughly 1 hour). There are also a few direct long-distance buses from Seoul's Central City Terminal to Gangjin, but they run only a handful of times a day and take around 4.5 hours — check the exact schedule before you book, since bus timetables change.
  • From Gangjin Bus Terminal to the island: Take a local "Nongeochon" (rural area) bus heading toward Maryang and get off at Jeodu Village bus stop, right by the suspension bridge entrance. A taxi from the terminal is the easier option if you're short on time — it only takes about 10–15 minutes.
  • By car: If you're renting a car for a Jeollanam-do road trip, Gaudo Island has its own parking area right next to the bridge, which makes this one of the easiest ways to visit.

A few practical notes before you go: there are only a few small shops and cafés on the island, so bring water and snacks if you're planning to stay a while. The walking trail has little shade in some sections, so sun protection matters in summer. And since this is a quiet, mostly local destination, don't expect much English signage — downloading a translation app or saving the island's name in Korean (가우도) to show a taxi driver will make things much smoother.

💬 Been to Gaudo Island or another hidden spot in Jeollanam-do? Tell us about it in the comments below!
meta_description: Gaudo Island in Gangjin: walk a suspension bridge to a car-free island with a coastal trail, zip line, and quiet bay views.
